assessment.overall_rationale: The two candidate sets describe essentially the same three biological modules for program P21 (core mevalonate/cholesterol enzymatic pathway, SREBP2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional regulation, and MASLD-context lipid/cholesterol coupling), with modules 1-1, 2-2, and 3-3 as clear high-similarity matches and cross-pairs showing only weak contextual overlap from shared genes/regulators without shared core mechanism.

pair_scores.rationale: Both catalogue the same complete mevalonate-to-cholesterol enzymatic cascade in hepatocytes with near-identical gene lists and mechanism.
Shares only the Erg28 scaffold gene; left is the enzymatic biosynthesis cascade while right's core mechanism is SREBP2 transcriptional control.
Only Acat2 overlaps and the right module's core focus (MASLD esterification/steatosis/export) differs entirely from left's biosynthetic enzyme cascade.
Left's core mechanism is SREBP2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional regulation, which right module 1 mentions only as an upstream regulator of its primarily enzymatic biosynthesis pathway.
Both describe the identical SCAP-SREBP2-INSIG1 axis co-regulating cholesterol genes, with Erg28 and Rdh11 as shared distinctive co-regulated targets.
Left's transcriptional control mechanism shares no meaningful mechanistic overlap with right's downstream MASLD lipid esterification/export module.
Acss2 acetyl-CoA provision is shared, but left's core focus on lipid-cholesterol export coupling (Dgat2/Mttp) is absent from right's primarily enzymatic biosynthesis module.
No mechanistic overlap between left's acetyl-CoA/lipid export coupling and right's transcriptional SREBP2 regulation core.

Both describe the same MASLD hepatic lipid-cholesterol homeostasis network sharing Dgat2/Mttp/Acat2 roles, though left emphasizes acetyl-CoA carbon provision while right adds esterification/steatosis regulators (Ddr2, Fads2).
